title: Launch Brief (Internal): Redwood Private Upgrade + Rollback (Beta → GA)
content:
Slide 1 — Title
Private Upgrade + Rollback Mechanism (Redwood Private)
Internal Launch Brief (Beta → GA)
Owners: Vivek (PM), Connor (Release Eng), Ethan (Control Plane), Sean (SRE), Marcus (Security)
Last updated: 2025-02-10

Speaker notes:
- This deck is for internal alignment on what we are shipping, how we are rolling it out, and what we are explicitly not promising in v1.
- Scope includes both VPC and on-prem/air-gapped packaging.


Slide 2 — Why now / the problem
Customer pain today:
- Upgrades are “runbook + heroics”; results vary across environments.
- Partial upgrades can wedge deployments (hard to diagnose; slow to recover).
- Limited rollback options; unclear when downgrade is safe.
- Air-gapped customers need consistent artifact integrity + import workflows.
- Support burden: troubleshooting is slow without a standard diagnostics bundle.

Business impact:
- Upgrade friction blocks expansions and renewals (security/compliance requirements).
- Higher SRE/support load during upgrade windows.

Speaker notes:
- We have at least two concrete signals: SUP-1842 (failed migration / stuck mid-upgrade) and SUP-1861 (air-gapped upgrade request requiring stronger process + tooling).


Slide 3 — Goals (what success looks like)
Product/engineering goals:
- Repeatable, deterministic upgrade workflow for Redwood Private.
- Pre-upgrade safety checks to catch obvious failure conditions.
- Automatic backup/snapshot of critical state + verification step.
- Well-defined rollback hooks + operator UX (manual + safe auto triggers).
- Strong observability and a standard diagnostics bundle.

Operator goals:
- Clear “what will happen” plan output before doing anything.
- Actionable remediation messages when prechecks fail.
- A documented, supportable rollback procedure.

Success metrics (beta → GA):
- ≥ 90% of beta upgrades complete without human intervention beyond follow-the-prompts.
- Rollback restores service health within target window (SLO to be finalized; initial target: < 30 minutes for typical VPC clusters).
- Diagnostics bundle generated in 100% of failed runs and attached/available for Support.

Speaker notes:
- We are not promising zero downtime universally, but we are designing safe sequencing to minimize downtime and avoid split-brain.


Slide 4 — Non-goals / explicit limitations (v1)
Not in scope:
- Re-architecting the private installer from scratch.
- A general-purpose customer GitOps system.
- Guaranteeing zero downtime in all environments.

Known limitations / “no surprises” language:
- Downgrade is constrained by data migrations: forward-only migrations block rollback.
- Rollback window is limited (policy-driven). “Roll back immediately” is different from “downgrade a week later.”
- Some environment-specific backup types may be optional (e.g., PV snapshots depend on storage class/snapshot support).

Speaker notes:
- We need consistent messaging to Sales/CS: rollback is supported with guardrails; it is not a blanket “downgrade anything anytime.”


Slide 5 — What’s shipping: capabilities overview
Installer UX:
- upgrade plan: show step graph + ordering, versions, and readiness gates.
- prechecks: pluggable checks w/ severity + remediation hints; JSON output for Support ingestion.
- upgrade apply: staged execution with health validation gates.
- rollback: guided command re-applies previous known-good versions and restores snapshots when safe.

Platform components (high-level):
- Control plane exposes component version reporting + correlation id propagation.
- Helm charts include ordering guarantees, readiness gates, and feature-flagged rollback hooks.
- Observability pack includes dashboards/alerts for upgrade execution.

Speaker notes:
- Call out “plan before apply” as a key shift. Operators should be able to understand exactly what will happen.


Slide 6 — Upgrade framework: phases and invariants
Phases (target behavior):
1) Preflight: gather environment info + compatibility checks + drift detection
2) Prechecks: fail fast on blocking conditions (k8s version, disk, permissions, storage class)
3) Backup: control plane DB snapshot + config/state backup (+ optional PV snapshots)
4) Apply: staged upgrades in safe order (control plane → gateways → runtime; exact ordering per design)
5) Validate: post-upgrade smoke tests + health checks; record status
6) Finalize: mark previous version as rollback target; emit summary + artifacts

Invariants (do not violate):
- Never proceed past a gate without recording upgrade state.
- Every run has a correlation id and produces a report + logs.
- If backup verification fails, abort and surface rollback guidance.
- Rollback is blocked when migrations are forward-only or schema is incompatible.

Speaker notes:
- The “state model” and failure-mode handling are the core of safety. If we can’t reason about state, we can’t safely recover.


Slide 7 — Rollback policy: what we support
Policy summary (operator-facing):
- Supported rollback is “return to previous known good” within a defined window and compatibility constraints.
- Rollback safety checks prevent destructive downgrades.
- If forward-only DB migrations were applied, rollback may be limited to restoring from snapshot taken pre-upgrade (if snapshot is available) or require Support/PS engagement.

Practical operator guidance:
- Prefer rollback immediately after detecting upgrade failure.
- Always keep the pre-upgrade snapshot until upgrade is validated + retention threshold is met.

Speaker notes:
- Messaging needs to be consistent across docs, installer prompts, and Support macros.


Slide 8 — Air-gapped (on-prem) delivery: offline upgrade bundles
Why it matters:
- Air-gapped customers require artifact integrity + provenance.

What’s included in the offline bundle:
- Signed manifest with versions, digests, and required components.
- Container images (or references + tooling to load into local registry), Helm charts, installer binary.
- Optional “compatibility matrix” payload to validate supported version skew.

Operator workflow (high level):
- Import bundle → verify signature → load images → run prechecks → plan → apply.

Failure handling:
- Verification failure is a hard stop with explicit guidance (do not allow “--force” bypass in GA).

Speaker notes:
- Security requirement: mandatory verification for on-prem. This is part of our trust story.


Slide 9 — Observability + diagnostics (Day-2)
New telemetry emitted:
- Structured logs per step (step id, duration, result, error class)
- Metrics: upgrade_attempts, upgrade_failures, rollback_triggers, step_duration_seconds
- Correlation id propagated into control plane logs to trace across services

Dashboards/alerts (SRE):
- Upgrade execution overview (success rate, failure reasons)
- Step duration anomalies (p95) and “stuck step” alerts
- Per-customer upgrade status panels (for managed support)

Diagnostics bundle (Support/PS):
- Precheck report (human + JSON)
- Step timing report + final summary
- Relevant k8s events, recent pod logs (scoped), installer logs
- Pointer to snapshot ids/backup locations (no secrets)

Speaker notes:
- “Diagnostics bundle exists” is not enough; it must be easy to collect and consistently formatted.


Slide 10 — Support readiness
What Support needs before beta:
- Support-facing runbook: triage checklist + how to interpret precheck failures.
- Known error catalog: mapping from installer error codes → next steps.
- Escalation path: when to involve Release Eng vs SRE vs Security.
- Macro / template for customer comms during a failed upgrade.

Enablement plan:
- 45-min enablement session w/ Support + PS (recorded)
- “How to collect diagnostics” short guide for customers (docs draft)

Owners:
- Dev Patel (Support enablement), Kira Thompson (docs), Owen Phillips (escalation playbook)

Speaker notes:
- Goal is to reduce ping-pong and shorten time-to-mitigation during maintenance windows.


Slide 11 — Release & gating: Beta criteria
Beta entry criteria (must-haves):
- Precheck framework in installer w/ severity + remediation hints.
- Backup step for control plane DB (snapshot + verify) wired into upgrade flow.
- Rollback command available with guardrails (blocks unsafe downgrades).
- Offline bundle import + signature verification available (on-prem track).
- Upgrade telemetry + diagnostics tarball produced.
- SRE dashboards live + initial alert thresholds set (conservative, avoid noise).

Beta guardrails:
- Beta only with PS/Solutions involvement.
- Upgrade windows scheduled; on-call coverage confirmed.
- No “surprise” schema migrations; migration policy reviewed.

Speaker notes:
- Beta is not “self-serve.” We want signal and safety first.


Slide 12 — GA criteria
GA readiness checklist (high level):
- Successful upgrades across test matrix (incl. failure injection) with documented outcomes.
- Rollback drill completion: at least 3 scenarios validated (image pull failure, disk full, schema mismatch).
- Docs: customer-facing day-2 upgrade guide + runbook finalized.
- Support: enablement complete; macros + escalation rules in place.
- Security: signing/verification process documented; audit logging for upgrade/rollback actions enabled.
- Compatibility matrix enforced in installer with explicit error messaging.

GA bar (operational):
- Upgrade SLOs defined for typical deployments; measurement in place.
- Incident process: upgrades can be tagged + linked to diagnostics automatically.

Speaker notes:
- GA means “Supportable at scale.” Tooling without process is not GA.


Slide 13 — Rollout stages and timeline (proposed)
Stage 0: Internal rehearsal
- Staging private environment: run full upgrade + induced failure + rollback
- Outcome: tune gates, timeouts, and messaging

Stage 1: Beta (1–2 customers)
- One VPC customer + one on-prem/air-gapped if available
- Weekly check-ins; capture precheck failures and backup timing

Stage 2: Limited GA
- Feature enabled for a wider set of Private customers with defined prerequisites
- Support load monitored; adjust alerting and runbooks

Stage 3: Broad GA
- Documented as default upgrade mechanism; deprecate legacy runbook paths where safe

Speaker notes:
- Exact dates in the PRD / GA sheet; this slide is stage framing.


Slide 14 — Risks / open questions
Key risks:
- Backup duration vs maintenance windows (esp. large DBs and slow storage).
- Snapshot permissions (IAM) and least-privilege setup in customer clouds.
- False positives in prechecks (operator trust issue).
- Forward-only migrations: policy enforcement and customer expectations.

Open questions to close before GA:
- Default retention for snapshots (by env) and recommended RPO/RTO language.
- How we surface “previous known good version” (control plane vs installer local state).
- Non-interactive operation: flags needed for CI/GitOps-ish customers (without endorsing full GitOps).

Speaker notes:
- Track these in the working spec + Linear; don’t let “nice to have” block safety-critical items.


Slide 15 — Ask / decision points
Decisions requested:
- Confirm v1 rollback policy wording (what’s officially supported) — PM + SRE + Security sign-off.
- Confirm beta customer selection criteria + required prerequisites.
- Confirm GA gating owners and the final checklist source of truth.

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Finalize runbook draft + error catalog outline
- Lock initial compatibility matrix ranges
- Schedule internal rehearsal + on-call coverage

Speaker notes:
- The most important “decision” is aligning expectations across PM/Eng/SRE/Support on rollback constraints.


Appendix — References (for internal reviewers)
- Confluence design overview: private upgrade framework + rollback policy
- Linear: PM-482 (PRD), ENG-2314..2324 (implementation + security)
- GitHub: installer PRs (plan/prechecks/backup/rollback/offline bundle/diagnostics)
- SRE runbook: private upgrade runbook
- Support tickets: SUP-1842, SUP-1861
